request.system: You are a strict claim verifier. You only trust the catalog facts given to you.
request.user:
Verify every factual claim in the campaign is grounded in the catalog facts. Fail if any claim is unsupported, exaggerated, or contradicts the facts.
Rules (from reviewer overrides):
- ANY mention of an out-of-stock product (stock 0) fails, whether or not the copy prompts purchase — no editorial exception.
- Numeric spec claims (lumens, hours, capacity, ratings) must match the catalog exactly; doubling or inflating a spec fails.
- Transferring an attribute from another product, or upgrading 'water-resistant' to 'waterproof', is a fabricated claim and fails.
- A comparative or superlative claim ('brightest', 'longest-lasting', 'most X') is scoped to the product type named in the claim and checked against the comparison set below: it fails if a same-type peer beats the subject on the compared attribute. Vague puffery ('great gear', 'toughest', 'best ever') with no measurable attribute is acceptable.
Catalog facts:
(no catalog products referenced)

Claims to verify:
(no explicit claims)

Body: Hey,

No big announcements this time — just a note to check in as the season moves along.

If you've been out recently, you know the conditions have been variable. Shoulder season has a way of humbling even well-planned trips. Layers you didn't think you'd need, water sources that weren't where the map said, campsites that looked better in photos.

We've been paying attention to what people are actually running into out there, and we're working on bringing in gear that speaks to those real situations — not the curated highlight-reel version of a trip, but the version where you're problem-solving at mile 14.

More specifics coming soon. In the meantime, if there's something you've been looking for and haven't found — a particular weight range, a feature set, a use case we haven't covered — reply to this email. We read them.

Thanks for being on the list. We'll keep it useful.

— The Team
Respond with ONLY a JSON object, no prose or code fences. Reason first, then decide — the verdict must follow from the reasoning. Use exactly this key order: {"reasoning": "<one sentence>", "evidence": ["<short quote or fact>", ...], "score": <float 0-1>, "verdict": "pass"|"fail"}.

response:
```json
{
  "reasoning": "The email contains no explicit factual claims about products, specifications, stock status, or comparative attributes that can be verified against catalog facts; it is general seasonal communication without product-specific assertions.",
  "evidence": [
    "No catalog products are referenced",
    "No numeric specs mentioned",
    "No comparative or superlative claims about products",
    "No product names or stock status mentioned",
    "Content is motivational and conversational without verifiable claims"
  ],
  "score": 1.0,
  "verdict": "pass"
}
```
